content:
As TV Time shut down last month, co-founder Antonio Pinto has announced the launch of a new TV and film tracking app called Bingers, with a stronger emphasis on social features. Here's what you need to know.

Bingers is now available for download

Whip Media had previously announced the closure of the TV and film tracking app TV Time, and one of the app's co-founders promptly announced the launch of Bingers, describing it as 'a fast and stylish watchlist, and also a fun community.'

According to TechCrunch, Bingers is available for download on iOS and Android, offering a spiritual successor for users who have yet to find a replacement — TV Time itself was once one of the most widely used TV and film tracking apps in the world.

Former TV Time users who saved their data via its export tool before the platform shut down can import the file into Bingers and continue tracking where they left off; users who did not export their data, or new users who have never used a TV and film tracking app, can start from scratch.

Bingers places great emphasis on community-driven features, such as user profiles, comments, episode ratings, GIFs, polls, and character popularity votes. Pinto told TechCrunch that these features are precisely what has long attracted users to TV Time:

For users who simply want a platform to keep track of the shows and movies they have watched, Bingers offers dedicated watchlists and viewing records. Similar to TV Time, it also displays upcoming episodes and a calendar of premiere dates, with a countdown feature showing how many days remain until the premiere.

Bingers is available for free download on the App Store, with no in-app purchases at the moment.
